title: Two Kinds of Tidy

pre.en: What happens when Lily opens the hall cupboard?
pre.zh: Lily 打开门厅的柜子时发生了什么？
options: Lots of things fall on her head.

intro: 兄妹俩的对话：Lily 住进小陈家没多久，就受不了他的乱。两人一边吵一边翻旧账：小时候的小陈可是出了名的整洁。读的时候留意 used to：说「以前常常、以前是」，现在已经不这样了；否定和疑问是 didn't use to、Did you use to …? 结尾有个小笑点。

sentences.en: Chen, you leave mugs lying around everywhere.
sentences.zh: 哥，你的杯子到处乱放。
sentences.speaker: Lily

sentences.en: I've counted four in the living room and one in your sock drawer.
sentences.zh: 客厅里我数了，有四个，你放袜子的抽屉里还有一个。

sentences.en: The post has been piling up by the door since I arrived.
sentences.zh: 我来了以后，门口的信就越堆越多。

sentences.en: And yesterday I found your gas bill under a pizza box, completely by chance.
sentences.zh: 昨天我还在一个披萨盒底下翻出了你的煤气账单，纯属碰巧。

sentences.en: I usually do the washing-up on Sundays.
sentences.zh: 我一般周日洗碗。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: The mugs are just waiting their turn.
sentences.zh: 那些杯子只是在排队等着。

sentences.en: And honestly, that gas bill's perfectly safe under the pizza box.
sentences.zh: 再说了，煤气账单压在披萨盒底下安全得很。

sentences.en: You didn't use to be like this.
sentences.zh: 你以前可不这样。
sentences.speaker: Lily

sentences.en: When you were ten, you used to fold your socks and line up your pencils by colour.
sentences.zh: 你十岁那会儿，袜子都叠得整整齐齐，铅笔还按颜色排好。

sentences.en: Mum used to show your room to her friends when they came round.
sentences.zh: 妈的朋友来家里，她总要带人家参观你的房间。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I also used to have a mum who tidied up after me every single day.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那时候我还有个妈天天跟在后面帮我收拾呢。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: Did you use to make your own bed when you were ten?
sentences.zh: 你十岁的时候自己叠被子吗？

sentences.en: Every morning.
sentences.zh: 每天早上都叠。
sentences.speaker: Lily

sentences.en: I still do.
sentences.zh: 现在也是。

sentences.en: Nurses hardly ever leave a bed unmade.
sentences.zh: 护士哪有让床乱着的。

sentences.en: Look, the mugs drive me mad, but I'm not trying to change your whole life.
sentences.zh: 听着，那些杯子快把我逼疯了，但我也没想改造你整个人生。

sentences.en: Can you meet me halfway?
sentences.zh: 咱们各让一步，行不行？

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 行吧。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: But am I allowed to keep one mug on my desk?
sentences.zh: 那我桌上能留一个杯子吗？

sentences.en: To be honest, my standards went down a bit when I moved in with Tom.
sentences.zh: 说实话，跟 Tom 合租以后，我的标准是降了点。

sentences.en: One mug.
sentences.zh: 就一个。
sentences.speaker: Lily

sentences.en: And here's the rule: everything gets put away before bed.
sentences.zh: 规矩是：睡觉前所有东西都得收好。

sentences.en: On Saturday, we're clearing out the hall cupboard together, because I can't even open it.
sentences.zh: 周六咱俩一起把门厅那个柜子清一清，我连柜门都打不开。

sentences.en: Look on the bright side — you'll probably find things you forgot you had.
sentences.zh: 往好处想——说不定能翻出你自己都忘了的东西。

sentences.en: What's wrong with the hall cupboard?
sentences.zh: 门厅的柜子怎么了？
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: Feel free to have a quick look at it now.
sentences.zh: 你现在就可以去看一眼。

sentences.en: It's very organised.
sentences.zh: 里面整整齐齐的。

sentences.en: Ow!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！
sentences.speaker: Lily

sentences.en: An umbrella, a tennis racket, two old trainers and about forty plastic bags have just fallen on my head!
sentences.zh: 一把伞、一个网球拍、两只旧球鞋，还有差不多四十个塑料袋，全砸我头上了！

sentences.en: That's not mess, Lily.
sentences.zh: 那不叫乱，Lily。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: It's a system.
sentences.zh: 这叫乱中有序。

cards.note: to leave things in places where they should not be, instead of putting them away
cards.tip: lying 是 lie（躺、放着）的 -ing，不是「说谎」；英式也说 lying about。
cards.example: Don't leave your keys lying around — you'll lose them again.

cards.note: 英式说法，美式说 mail；寄信是 post a letter。
to become a large amount, often because you have not dealt with it
cards.tip: 可以说东西，也可以说事情：The work is piling up。名词是 a pile of（一堆）。
cards.example: My emails always pile up when I'm on holiday.

cards.note: 英国的水、电、煤气分开收费，统称 bills：pay the bills。
in a way that was not planned
cards.tip: 前面可以加 completely、purely 加强；反义是 on purpose（第 1 课）。
cards.example: We met by chance at the station.

cards.note: to wash the plates, cups and pans after a meal
cards.tip: 英式说法，固定用 do，不说 make the washing-up；美式说 do the dishes。洗衣服是 do the washing。
cards.example: You cooked, so I'll do the washing-up.

cards.note: 叠衣服：fold the washing；反义 unfold。
to make a place clean and neat by putting things where they belong
un- 表示「没」：made 是铺好的，unmade 是乱着的。

cards.zh: 快把某人逼疯；让人受不了
cards.note: to annoy someone very much
cards.tip: 英式口语；mad 在这里是「疯」不是「生气」。也说 drive sb crazy。
cards.example: The noise from the building site is driving me mad.

cards.note: to agree to some of what another person wants so that you can both agree
cards.tip: meet 的过去式是 met；也可以说 meet in the middle。
cards.example: They wanted £500 and we offered £300, so we met them halfway.

cards.note: to have permission to do something
cards.tip: 后面接动词原形；问能不能做时比 Can I…? 更像在问规矩。
cards.example: You're not allowed to park here after six.

cards.note: used before you say what you really think, especially something the listener may not like
常用复数：have high standards（要求高）。
if a computer system goes down, it stops working
to put something back in the place where it is usually kept
cards.tip: 代词放中间：put it away，不说 put away it；put 的三种形式都是 put。
cards.example: Can you put the shopping away while I make tea?

cards.zh: 清理（把不要的东西清出去）
cards.note: to make a place tidy by removing things you do not want
cards.tip: 比 tidy up 动静大：tidy up 是收拾整齐，clear out 是把东西搬出来、扔掉一批。
cards.example: We cleared out the garage and found three old bikes.

cards.zh: 往好处想；看到好的一面
cards.note: to find something good in a bad situation
used to tell someone that they can do something if they want to

cards.text: have a quick look at sth
cards.note: to look at something for a short time
网球、羽毛球拍用 racket；乒乓球拍是 bat。
